description:
Rolling replay segment buffer + on-disk storage layout for the v2 native/helper replay engine. Replaces the v1.1.0 MediaRecorder VP8/WebM replay buffer. Design only — no code.

Full design record: N-005. Summary in `.story/project-state.md` under "v2.0.0 rolling replay segment buffer (T-006)". Locked decisions below.

Storage model: **one fMP4 segment file per GOP, ~2 s, written incrementally as fragments arrive, atomically committed at GOP boundary.** Rejected alternatives: in-memory-only ring (RAM ceiling reintroduces v1.1.0 bound problem), one file per 250 ms fragment (1200 files / 5 min, no upside), larger N-GOP segments (eviction loses too much head, no upside).

Directory layout (Linux): `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/replay/<sessionId>/` containing `init.mp4` (init segment, written once, fsync'd), `manifest.json` (clean-shutdown digest), `index.jsonl` (append-only event log), `current.txt` (recovery hint), `pid.lock` (live-session exclusive lock), `segments/seg-XXXXXXXX.m4s` (committed segments), `segments/seg-XXXXXXXX.partial` (in-flight). Windows: same shape under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.

Atomic write/rotate protocol: fragments appended to `.partial`; at GOP boundary fsync, atomic rename to `.m4s`, append + fsync `index.jsonl`, parent-dir fsync, update `current.txt`, run eviction pass. fsync only at commit (0.5 Hz), never per-fragment.

Replay window presets: **30 s, 60 s, 2 m, 5 m, 10 m.** Underlying `replay_window_seconds` accepts [10, 1800]. 10 min is the longest default; longer requires advanced settings.

Eviction policy: two limits in parallel, first tripped wins. Window limit (primary): committed duration > `replay_window_seconds + 1 GOP` headroom. Byte limit (safety net): bytes > `disk_cap_bytes` (default `max(window_s × bitrate / 8 × 1.5, 1 GB)` clamped to 8 GB ceiling). Eviction runs AFTER commit, never before. Per-segment granularity. Pinned segments cannot be evicted.

Save snapshot model (the v1.1.0 freeze-during-save fix as contract): on `replay.save(N)` — (1) force IDR via `encoder.force_idr_now()`, (2) drain to next IDR-fronted fragment (≤ 250 ms), (3) commit the in-flight segment, (4) pin a `ReplaySnapshot { snapshot_id, init_segment_path, segments: Vec<SegmentRef>, trim_start_pts_90k, trim_end_pts_90k, codec, timescale, width, height, has_discontinuity, discontinuity_at_pts_90k }`, (5) return immediately. Capture, encode, and segment writes continue uninterrupted. T-007 reads pinned files on a separate task. `replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)` ends the pin; deferred evictions then unlink.

Crash safety: committed `.m4s` files survive (atomic rename + fsync + parent-dir fsync); `.partial` files are always discarded on recovery; `init.mp4` and `manifest.json` are durable. Recovery triage layers: manifest > JSONL replay > filesystem scan with fMP4-header parse for orphan `.m4s` files. User sees recovered sessions as an optional save prompt.

Format-change handling: encoder forces IDR + `discontinuity: true` on `formatChanged` (N-004). T-006 closes current segment, opens new one with `discontinuity = true`. Snapshot exposes `has_discontinuity` + crossing PTS list. T-007 re-encodes across crossings with libx264 only.

Failure modes catalogued: `segment-sink-pressure`, `segment-sink-disk-full`, `segment-sink-slow`, `segment-sink-fsync-failed`, `segment-sink-rename-failed`, `segment-sink-state-dir-unwritable`, `segment-sink-vanished`. Each surfaces a typed `sessionLost` with the last 30 s of T-006 diagnostics dumped into `$XDG_STATE_HOME/.../diagnostics/<sessionId>.json`.

I/O budget at worst case (4K60 / 50 Mbps): 6.25 MB/s sustained, ~1.56 MB per fragment, one fsync per 12.5 MB, file-create rate 0.5/s, ~150 inodes for 5-min buffer, ~850 KB in-memory index for 10-min buffer. Comfortable on NVMe, SATA SSD, modern HDD, and USB 3.0 external. USB 2.0 is the documented boundary at 4K60.

Diagnostics counters (1 Hz + on transitions): `fragments_received_total`, `fragments_dropped_orphan_total`, `segments_committed_total`, `segments_evicted_total`, `segments_pinned_count`, `segments_count_on_disk`, `bytes_on_disk_total`, `bytes_written_total`, `evict_bytes_freed_total`, `evict_blocked_by_pin_total`, `disk_write_latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}`, `fsync_latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}`, `rename_latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}`, `push_fragment_pending_events_total`, `back_pressure_sustained_ms`, `save_snapshots_taken_total`, `save_snapshots_active`, `partial_segment_recovered_total`, `partial_segment_discarded_total`, `formatchange_segments_total`, `buffer_window_seconds_observed`, `buffer_bytes_pct_of_cap`. Pairs with N-003 §14 and N-004 §16 to triangulate where any dropped frame happened.

v1.1.0 freeze-during-save invariant preserved by four structural choices: snapshot is paths not bytes; eviction defers to pins (not the reverse); encoder ↔ sink async with back-pressure (live capture prioritised); force-IDR-on-save bounded to ≤ 250 ms. Contract: `replay.save(...)` returns within ≤ 250 ms + encoder fragment latency, capture rate identical before/during/after.

Audio future: parallel `audio/aud-XXXXXXXX.m4s` directory slot reserved; audio commits aligned to video segment boundaries; snapshot extends with `audio_segments`. Audio encode itself is a separate ticket.

T-007 consumption contract (binding): T-007 receives `ReplaySnapshot`, reads on a separate task, calls `replay.snapshot_release` on completion. Concat + faststart for trim-on-IDR; head/tail GOP re-encode with libx264 for trim-mid-GOP; libx264 re-encode across each discontinuity; libx264 full re-encode under Maximum-compatibility toggle. T-006 never reads snapshot files itself.

Out of scope: audio encode, multi-stream replay, user-facing replay-window UI design (T-008), file encryption, cloud upload, manual eviction, pause/resume design beyond the trait's existing semantics. Open implementation items (non-blocking): fMP4 muxer = ffmpeg `movenc`, Windows `FlushFileBuffers` semantics, `statvfs`/`GetDiskFreeSpaceEx` for pre-session disk probe, `index.jsonl` compaction at clean shutdown only.
title: Design rolling replay segment buffer
